theory.intro: Standard deviation only responds to changes that alter how far the values sit from their **mean**. Two changes come up again and again: shifting every value by the same amount, and adding one new value.
facts: Adding or subtracting the same constant to **every** value shifts the **mean** by that constant.
This is true no matter how large or small the constant is.
If every value in a dataset is identical, there is no spread at all, so $\sigma_x = 0$.
steps: Identify what changes about the dataset
Decide the effect on the mean
Decide the effect on the standard deviation

workedExamples.question_text:
The four test scores are $11,15,18,24$.
(a) Use a calculator to find the mean and population standard deviation. Give standard deviations correct to $2$ decimal places.
(b) Instead, increase every original score by $3$. State the new mean and standard deviation.
(c) Instead, decrease every original score by $5$. State the new mean and standard deviation.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Enter $11,15,18,24$ into statistics mode.
Read $\bar{x}=17$ and $\sigma_x=4.743416\ldots\approx4.74$.
(b) Each score and the mean increase by $3$.
New mean $=17+3=20$.
The spread is unchanged, so $\sigma_x\approx4.74$.
(c) Each score and the mean decrease by $5$.
New mean $=17-5=12$.
The spread is unchanged, so $\sigma_x\approx4.74$.
A shift changes the mean, not the standard deviation.

workedExamples.question_text:
The five scores $9,12,16,18,20$ have mean $15$ and population standard deviation $4$. Consider each change separately.
(a) Add one new score of $15$. Explain what happens to the standard deviation.
(b) Add one new score of $1$. Explain what happens to the standard deviation.
(c) Replace all five original scores by $15$. State the new mean and explain why the standard deviation is zero.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The new score equals the mean, so its distance from the mean is $0$.
There is less spread overall, so the standard deviation decreases.
(b) The new score is $15-1=14$ below the original mean.
This distance is much greater than the current standard deviation of $4$.
Adding this score increases the spread, so the standard deviation increases.
(c) Every score is now $15$, so the mean remains $15$.
There is no spread, so $\sigma_x=0$.

foundation.question_text:
A team's $5$ employees have a mean weekly wage of $\$620$ and population standard deviation $\$45$.
Each employee is given a $\$30$ pay rise.
State the new mean wage, and explain why the standard deviation is unchanged.
foundation.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = 620 + 30$
$= \$650$
Every wage shifted by the same $\$30$, so the spread between wages — and therefore $\sigma_x = \$45$ — has not changed.

foundation.question_text:
A team's $6$ employees have a mean weekly wage of $\$580$ and population standard deviation $\$38$.
Due to a cost-saving measure, every employee's wage is cut by $\$15$.
State the new mean wage, and explain why the standard deviation is unchanged.
foundation.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = 580 - 15$
$= \$565$
Every wage shifted down by the same $\$15$, so the spread between wages — and therefore $\sigma_x = \$38$ — has not changed.

foundation.question_text:
A gym class's $6$ members have a mean of $24$ push-ups and population standard deviation $3.2$ push-ups in a fitness test.
In the retest, every member does $4$ more push-ups.
State the new mean, and explain why the standard deviation is unchanged.
foundation.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = 24 + 4$
$= 28$
Every member's count shifted up by the same $4$ push-ups, so the spread between them — and therefore $\sigma_x = 3.2$ — has not changed.

foundation.question_text:
Five employees have wages with mean $\$600$ and population standard deviation $\$50$.
A new employee joins earning exactly $\$600$.
Explain why adding this employee decreases the standard deviation.
foundation.solution_text:
The new employee's wage, $\$600$, is exactly at the mean, so its distance from the mean is $\$0$ — far less than the current standard deviation of $\$50$.
Including this value pulls the average distance from the mean down, so $\sigma_x$ decreases.

foundation.question_text:
Six gym members have a mean of $22$ push-ups and population standard deviation $2.8$ push-ups.
A new member joins the class and manages only $4$ push-ups.
Explain why adding this member increases the standard deviation.
foundation.solution_text:
The new member's count, $4$, is $18$ push-ups from the mean of $22$ — far more than the current standard deviation of $2.8$ push-ups.
Including this far-below-average value pulls the average distance from the mean up, so $\sigma_x$ increases.

foundation.question_text:
A manager currently pays $6$ staff different casual rates, with population standard deviation $\$62$.
She proposes a flat rate: every staff member will be paid exactly the same rate, equal to the current mean rate.
What will the new standard deviation be?
Explain.
foundation.solution_text:
$\sigma_x = 0$
When every staff member is paid the same rate, there is no spread at all between the wages.

development.question_text:
Six employees at a small business earn weekly wages of $\$520$, $\$610$, $\$480$, $\$700$, $\$550$ and $\$640$.
Calculate the mean, correct to $1$ decimal place, and the population standard deviation, correct to $2$ decimal places, of these wages.
Every employee is then given a $\$25$ pay rise.
State the new mean, and explain why $\sigma_x$ is unchanged.
development.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = 583.3333...$
$\approx \$583.3$
$\sigma_x = 74.5356...$
$\approx \$74.54$
After the rise, the new mean is $583.3 + 25 = \$608.3$.
$\sigma_x$ stays $\$74.54$, since every wage shifted by the same amount and the spread between them has not changed.

development.question_text:
In a fitness challenge, $5$ gym members complete $22$, $18$, $25$, $20$ and $24$ push-ups.
Calculate the mean and the population standard deviation of this dataset, correct to $2$ decimal places.
In the next round, a stricter rule costs every member $3$ push-ups from their count.
State the new mean, and explain why $\sigma_x$ is unchanged.
development.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = 21.8$
$\sigma_x = 2.5612...$
$\approx 2.56$
After the penalty, the new mean is $21.8 - 3 = 18.8$.
$\sigma_x$ stays $2.56$, since every count shifted down by the same amount and the spread between them has not changed.

development.question_text:
Five employees earn wages of $\$500$, $\$600$, $\$550$, $\$650$ and $\$700$.
Calculate the mean and the population standard deviation of these wages, correct to $2$ decimal places.
A new employee then joins, earning exactly $\$600$.
Explain why adding this employee decreases the standard deviation.
development.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = \$600$
$\sigma_x = 70.7107...$
$\approx \$70.71$
The new employee's wage, $\$600$, equals the mean, so its distance from the mean is $\$0$.
Adding a value at the mean reduces the spread overall, so $\sigma_x$ decreases.

development.question_text:
Five gym members complete $20$, $17$, $23$, $19$ and $21$ push-ups.
Calculate the mean and the population standard deviation of this dataset, correct to $2$ decimal places.
A new member then joins and manages only $2$ push-ups.
Explain why adding this member increases the standard deviation.
development.solution_text:
$\overline{x} = 20$
$\sigma_x = 2.00$
The new member's count is $20-2=18$ push-ups below the original mean.
This distance is much greater than the current standard deviation of $2.00$.
Adding this value increases the spread, so $\sigma_x$ increases.

development.question_text:
A payroll analyst is considering four possible changes to a company's wage dataset, which currently has mean $\$610$ and $\sigma_x = \$52$.
(i) Every wage increases by $\$40$.
(ii) A new employee joins earning $\$610$.
(iii) A new employee joins earning $\$1450$.
(iv) Every wage decreases by $\$25$.
For each change, state whether $\sigma_x$ increases, decreases, or stays the same.
development.solution_text:
(i) Adding the same amount to every wage does not change the spread, so $\sigma_x$ stays the same.
(ii) The new wage equals the current mean, so it pulls the average distance from the mean down: $\sigma_x$ decreases.
(iii) The new wage is far above the current mean, so it pulls the average distance from the mean up: $\sigma_x$ increases.
(iv) Subtracting the same amount from every wage does not change the spread, so $\sigma_x$ stays the same.

development.question_text:
A gym's fitness-test results have a mean of $24$ push-ups and $\sigma_x = 3.5$ push-ups.
Two changes are proposed. Consider each separately.
(i) Every member does $3$ more push-ups in the retest. State the new mean and standard deviation.
(ii) A new member joins who can do exactly $24$ push-ups. Explain what happens to the standard deviation.
development.solution_text:
(i) Every count shifts up by $3$.
The new mean is $24+3=27$.
The spread is unchanged, so $\sigma_x$ stays $3.5$.
(ii) The new count equals the current mean, so its distance from the mean is $0$.
Adding this value reduces the spread overall, so $\sigma_x$ decreases.

mastery.question_text:
A company's six senior staff earn weekly wages of $\$500$, $\$540$, $\$580$, $\$620$, $\$660$ and $\$700$.
Calculate the population standard deviation of these wages, correct to $2$ decimal places.
Each staff member then receives a $\$35$ pay increase.
Explain the effect of this increase on the standard deviation.
mastery.solution_text:
Enter the six wages into statistics mode.
$\sigma_x=68.3130\ldots$
$\sigma_x\approx\$68.31$.
Every wage increases by the same $\$35$, so the spread is unchanged.
The population standard deviation remains $\$68.31$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

mastery.question_text:
In a fitness challenge, $5$ gym members complete $40$, $45$, $50$, $55$ and $60$ push-ups.
Calculate the mean and the population standard deviation of this dataset, correct to $2$ decimal places.
Instead, suppose every member had completed $50$ push-ups.
State what would happen to the mean and explain why the standard deviation would be zero.
mastery.solution_text:
Enter the five counts into statistics mode.
$\overline{x}=50$.
$\sigma_x=7.0711\ldots$
$\sigma_x\approx7.07$.
If every member had completed $50$ push-ups, the mean would remain $50$.
All counts would be identical, so there would be no spread.
The standard deviation would be $0$.

mastery.question_text:
A gym's $5$ members complete a push-up test: $24$, $20$, $27$, $22$ and $26$ push-ups.
Calculate the population standard deviation of this dataset, correct to $2$ decimal places.
Consider each change to the original results separately.
(a) In the retest, every member does $2$ more push-ups than before. State the new standard deviation without recalculating from scratch, and explain your reasoning.
(b) A new member joins the original group, completing only $5$ push-ups. Explain what happens to the standard deviation.
mastery.solution_text:
Enter the five original counts into statistics mode.
$\sigma_x=2.5612\ldots$
$\sigma_x\approx2.56$.
(a) Every count increases by the same $2$, so the spread is unchanged.
The standard deviation remains $2.56$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
(b) The original mean is $23.8$.
The new score is $23.8-5=18.8$ below this mean.
This distance is much greater than the original standard deviation of $2.56$.
Adding this score increases the spread, so the standard deviation increases.
